title: Non-decreasing Array
description:
# Non-decreasing Array

Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if it can become non-decreasing by modifying **at most one element**. A modification may replace one array value with any integer.

An array is non-decreasing when `nums[i] <= nums[i + 1]` for every valid index `i`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [4,2,3]
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** Change the first value from 4 to 1, giving [1,2,3].

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [4,2,1]
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** At least two positions would need to change before the array could become non-decreasing.

## Constraints:

* `n == nums.length`
* `1 <= n <= 10^4`
* `-10^5 <= nums[i] <= 10^5`

solutions.name: Greedy Single Pass Repair
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan adjacent pairs from left to right and count how many times `nums[i] > nums[i + 1]`. On the first violation, repair the local pair in place: lower the left value when it can still fit after the previous value; otherwise raise the right value.

## Key Insight

The repair direction is forced by `nums[i - 1]`. If `nums[i - 1] <= nums[i + 1]`, lowering `nums[i]` preserves the checked prefix. Otherwise the only possible one-edit repair is to raise `nums[i + 1]` to `nums[i]`. A second violation proves that one edit is not enough.

## Complexity Analysis

The scan visits each element once, so the running time is O(n). The algorithm mutates the input array but uses only O(1) extra storage.

solutions.name: Local Violation Certificate
solutions.description:
## Approach

Find the unique decreasing adjacent pair, if it exists. If there is more than one decreasing pair, return `false`. For a single pair at index `i`, decide whether one of the two endpoints can be changed by checking only the neighbors around that pair.

## Key Insight

Any successful one-edit solution must fix the first violation `nums[i] > nums[i + 1]` by changing either `nums[i]` or `nums[i + 1]`. Changing the left value is possible when `i == 0` or `nums[i - 1] <= nums[i + 1]`; changing the right value is possible when `i + 1` is the last index or `nums[i] <= nums[i + 2]`.

## Complexity Analysis

The array is scanned once and only constant state is kept, so the time complexity is O(n) and the extra space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: Prefix Suffix Sorted Certificates
solutions.description:
## Approach

Precompute whether every prefix and every suffix is already non-decreasing. Then try each index as the one value to change and ask whether the unchanged left prefix and right suffix are valid and whether some replacement value can fit between its two neighbors.

## Key Insight

For index `i`, the modified value only has to satisfy `nums[i - 1] <= value <= nums[i + 1]` when both neighbors exist. Prefix and suffix certificates prove that all other pairs are already valid, so the problem reduces to checking whether that interval is non-empty.

## Complexity Analysis

Building the two certificate arrays and scanning candidate indices are both linear. The algorithm uses O(n) time and O(n) extra space.

solutions.name: Virtual First-Violation Edits
solutions.description:
## Approach

Locate the first decreasing adjacent pair. If no pair exists, the answer is already true. Otherwise, test the only two meaningful edits without changing the array: pretend the left endpoint was lowered to the right value, or pretend the right endpoint was raised to the left value.

## Key Insight

The first violation must disappear after one edit, so changing any index outside that adjacent pair cannot help. A virtual validation scan for the two candidate edits gives a compact correctness oracle while keeping the input unchanged.

## Complexity Analysis

The method performs one scan to find the first violation and up to two validation scans. This is still O(n) time, with O(1) extra space.
